subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — shoulder scaling & SLO-aware bursting for Nebula Tech
messages:

Cc: Arman Patel <arman@nebula-tech.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning for upcoming launch (forecast + burst ask)

Diego,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. A quick follow-up from our side: Nebula is planning a beta launch mid-July and we expect a significant ramp around feature release windows — roughly 3x baseline QPS for short windows (10–30m) several times per day.

We need help validating the Dedicated sizing you proposed and locking in an autoscale/burst policy that keeps our latency P99 under 350ms while keeping committed spend predictable. Key asks:
- Recommended baseline reserved pool (GPU type & count) for our 200k monthly active sessions profile
- Headroom / burst headroom multiplier and brief on how burst credits would be billed
- Eviction/priority rules if we hit cluster contention (we run two priority classes: interactive & batch)

Attached is our updated forecast (capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx). Can we do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to align on SLO-aware bursting and contractual guardrails?

Thanks,
Lina Morales
Director, Infrastructure
Nebula Tech

- capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Lina Morales <lina@nebula-tech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for upcoming launch (forecast + burst ask)

Lina — thanks for the forecast and the clear asks.

High level summary up front: we can meet your P99 target with a mix of reserved A100-80GB capacity for baseline + an ephemeral H100 shoulder pool for short bursts, combined with SLO-aware routing that favors interactive traffic. The details below are my initial take; Ben / Olga — tagging for ops + procurement/legal validation.

Baseline recommendation (quick):
- Reserved: 8x A100-80GB (serve baseline steady-state with room for predictable growth)
- Shoulder (burst): ephemeral H100 slab sized for ~2.5x single-GPU throughput, configured as preemptible instances with a soft cap (max burst concurrency)
- Headroom multiplier: 1.8x for standard bursts; for feature-flagged launches we can grant a temporary 2.5x uplift with explicit time window and crediting

Autoscale policy highlights:
- SLO-aware routing: interactive requests (priority class) get KV cache priming and prefetched KV shards; batch jobs are put into lower-weight queues during contention.
- Scale triggers: token-inference queue depth + median token latency crossing 200ms for 30s window -> scale up; cooldown 120s; scale-down only after 4 minutes of stable low load to avoid oscillation.
- Eviction: preemptible shoulder pool evicts lowest-priority batch tasks first. We can offer a cross-tenant protected slab for Nebula's critical lanes as an optional add-on.

Billing / burst credits model (proposal):
- Reserved capacity billed monthly at committed rate (standard).
- Burst usage billed at a blended rate with capped daily burn for negotiated launch windows; we can also offer burst credits equal to 20% of monthly committed spend for the first quarter of the launch.

Next steps:
1) Ben — can you validate the GPU mix feasibility & rough cluster placement for these numbers?
2) Olga — we need a short clause describing temporary burst crediting and maximum daily burst cap for the SLA appendix.
3) Lina — confirm a good time tomorrow (I have 10:00–11:30 PT free).

Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (uploaded to shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/Nebula-Capacity-2027)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, Lina Morales <lina@nebula-tech.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for upcoming launch (technical follow-up)

Diego / Lina — quick ops reality check from infra:

GPU mix & placement
- A100-80GB reserved is fine for baseline throughput. For short 10–30m bursts, H100 preemptible nodes give better perf/cost if you configure per-GPU concurrency correctly.
- We recommend tuning per-GPU concurrency to 2–3 interactive sessions for H100 in the shoulder pool (lower for long-running batch).

Autoscaling knobs (technical):
- Trigger sources: we should combine (1) queue length (requests in-flight), (2) liveliness of KV cache hit rate drop, and (3) rising P50/P95 token latencies. A simple lat-lag hybrid dramatically reduces noise compared to raw CPU/GPU utilization.
- Cooldowns: scale-up immediate; scale-down after 4m stable; ensure a minimum replica floor to avoid thrashing (min replicas = reserved baseline).
- Eviction/priority: we already support per-route weights; implement a preempt priority token that marks batch tasks as evictable after tenant-provided TTL.

Operational guardrails
- Maximum burst window length: default 1 hour rolling across 24h to prevent sustained overage.
- Graceful degradation policy: if shoulder pool depleted, fallback to a smaller CPU-backed model that keeps throughput with higher latency (best-effort) rather than outright rejecting requests.

I'll sketch a quick ops diagram and capacity table (by GPU type) and drop it into the Drive.

Ben Carter
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment note: I referenced the capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx and will add an ops sheet mapping request shapes -> preferred GPU types.

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: lina@nebula-tech.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for upcoming launch (procurement & SLA items)

Lina / Diego — from contracts & procurement: a few practical items to surface before we lock terms.

SLA appendix items we need signed:
- Maximum daily burst cap (we propose a soft cap and a hard cap): soft cap = 1.5x daily expected consumption (can use burst credits), hard cap = 3x (excess billed at negotiated overage rate).
- Temporary launch uplift clause: define start/end window, with automatic reversion to baseline after end time. We will not auto-extend without written approval.
- Runbook & incident channels: add Redwood on-call rotation + Nebula primary contact + escalation matrix (DocuSign link below).

Procurement / billing ops
- For the launch quarter we can apply a 20% burst credit (one-time) against Nebula's committed monthly spend; credit redemption rules will be in the SLA appendix.
- Please confirm the purchase order cadence; renewals@nebula-tech.com should receive the DocuSign bundle for countersign.

I've attached a proposed signed SLA stub for our internal sign-off (proposed_sla_dod_signed.pdf) and will include the standard burst-credit wording. Diego — please confirm if we should proceed with the soft/hard cap thresholds above or propose alternate numbers after Ben's capacity table.

Olga Petrov
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
